learn.plain: Chips used to get better mainly by shrinking. Now they improve by stacking, smarter packaging, faster memory and new materials. The roadmap is a best guess that gets revised every year. Some bets could go well or badly, so exploring several futures is more honest than drawing one line.
learn.engineer: Through 2030 most density gains come from shorter standard cells, backside power and CFET rather than gate-pitch scaling, which imec expects to stay near 42 nm from A10 to A5. Beyond that, 2D channels, Hyper-NA EUV and 3D integration are the main levers, while system-level gains come from co-designing packaging, memory and interconnect. The scenario model treats efficiency as decaying yearly gains, and installed compute as the lower of its power and supply limits. Under most assumptions power binds by the 2030s.

quiz.q: Around when does imec expect CFET transistors to arrive?
quiz.why: It is a research projection, so it may move.

quiz.q: What did Intel ship first using High-NA EUV in 2026?
options: Select layers of Panther Lake processors on Intel 18A
quiz.why: ASML announced the milestone in July 2026.

quiz.q: On the roadmap, what does "Projection" mean?
options: A research forecast that may change
quiz.why: Shipping, announced, projection and outlook tell you how much to trust each item.

quiz.q: In the scenario planner, what most often limits total AI computing by the 2030s?
quiz.why: Under most settings power grows more slowly than the chips that could be built, so efficiency gains turn directly into more computing.

quiz.q: Which beyond-silicon technology is already in production in 2026?
quiz.why: NVIDIA Spectrum-X Photonics switches entered production in May 2026; the others are in research or prototypes.

quiz.q: What are quantum computers expected to speed up?
options: Specific problems such as chemistry and materials simulation
quiz.why: They are not general replacements for AI chips; first fault-tolerant machines are targeted around 2029.
